speech: This is Cre-den-sha, running live on Moh-nad testnet. [[slnc 140]] An issuer creates a credential, and anyone can verify it from a link, with nothing to install and no account.
sub: This is Credentia, running live on Monad testnet. An issuer creates a credential, and anyone can verify it from a link, with nothing to install and no account.

speech: The site walks you through it. [[slnc 100]] Issue a credential, share the link or the Q R code, and anyone can check it instantly.
sub: The site walks you through it. Issue a credential, share the link or the QR code, and anyone can check it instantly.

speech: Issuing starts here. [[slnc 100]] The form asks for a title, a recipient, their wallet address, and an optional expiry. It checks each field as you go, so a malformed address is caught straight away.
sub: Issuing starts here. The form asks for a title, a recipient, their wallet address, and an optional expiry. It checks each field as you go, so a malformed address is caught straight away.

speech: Issuing is for authorised issuers. [[slnc 100]] The page asks them to sign in with a passkey, and the registry only accepts issuers that pass our testnet identity gate. That gate is a stand-in for a real verifier, and the page says so.
sub: Issuing is for authorised issuers. The page asks them to sign in with a passkey, and the registry only accepts issuers that pass our testnet identity gate. That gate is a stand-in for a real verifier, and the page says so.

speech: Now the verifier's side. [[slnc 100]] This is a real credential, issued on Moh-nad testnet. Opening its link reads the registry directly. No account, no wallet.
sub: Now the verifier's side. This is a real credential, issued on Monad testnet. Opening its link reads the registry directly. No account, no wallet.

speech: The page shows four checks. [[slnc 100]] The link was read, the credential exists in the registry, the details match the on-chain fingerprint, and it's still active.
sub: The page shows four checks. The link was read, the credential exists in the registry, the details match the on-chain fingerprint, and it's still active.

speech: It shows who issued it, [[slnc 100]] and the verify button opens the transaction on the Moh-nad explorer, so anyone can confirm it independently.
sub: It shows who issued it, and the verify button opens the transaction on the Monad explorer, so anyone can confirm it independently.

speech: Every credential also has a receipt. [[slnc 100]] Its status, I D, issuer, the transaction hash, and the network.
sub: Every credential also has a receipt: its status, ID, issuer, the transaction hash, and the network.

speech: Now change one detail in the link, [[slnc 100]] here, the recipient name.
sub: Now change one detail in the link, here, the recipient name.

speech: The fingerprint no longer matches, [[slnc 140]] and Cre-den-sha tells the verifier not to rely on it.
sub: The fingerprint no longer matches, and Credentia tells the verifier not to rely on it.

speech: And when an issuer withdraws a credential, the page says revoked.
sub: And when an issuer withdraws a credential, the page says revoked.

speech: In our local setup, an Envee-oh indexer turns the registry's events into a timeline. [[slnc 160]] The credential was issued, then revoked.
sub: In our local setup, an Envio indexer turns the registry's events into a timeline. The credential was issued, then revoked.

speech: That's Cre-den-sha. [[slnc 250]] A credential anyone can verify, and nobody can quietly edit. [[slnc 200]] Live on Moh-nad testnet today, with the demo data labelled as such.
sub: That's Credentia. A credential anyone can verify, and nobody can quietly edit. Live on Monad testnet today, with the demo data labelled as such.
